clue.text: Withdraws nervously as a result of cage door being open?

definitions.meaning: the idiom for backing out of something through fear

definitions.text: as a result of cage door being open
definitions.meaning: the literal picture: hens escaping from an open coop

explanation.surface: Someone backs out in a panic, blamed on a cage door left open.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read twice: as the idiom for losing nerve, and literally as poultry wandering out of an open coop.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's nerve and pull out of a commitment is idiomatically to behave like a frightened fowl.

clue.text: Mark down answer in red biro?

indicators.note: the letter for answer is placed within the other two pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, stands for a red or communist
a biro is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A teacher marks an answer down in red biro.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE is a crossword stand-in for a red, after Che Guevara; a biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce the price or value of something is to make it less costly, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Problem when paper censors leader

indicators.note: censoring cuts out, here the first letter of the word for paper

parts.note: tissue is a thin kind of paper

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises when a newspaper suppresses its leading article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a newspaper's editorial, but it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter in dispute or a difficulty, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Races to install large electronic lights

indicators.note: the two letters are set up inside the word for races

parts.note: kinds are sorts or races of creature

explanation.surface: Races being run to install big electronic lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic lights' looks like one thing, maybe an e-reader; 'electronic' is just E and 'lights' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to set it burning, so kindles is a synonym for lights as a verb.

clue.text: End May with a lively celebration

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finishing the month of May with a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A name day is a feast of the saint one is named after, kept as a personal celebration in many countries.

clue.text: Bonded regularly with Don, secret society member

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word bonded

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word are kept
a don is a university teacher, also called a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Someone bonded routinely with a man called Don, a member of a secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a name; it is the Oxbridge sense of a college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a fraternal order with secret rituals, so one of them is a member of such a society.

clue.text: Restrict emblem Martinique takes up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read bottom to top
the answer is taken from within the run of letters of the two words

parts.note: the end of emblem and start of Martinique hold the letters, read backwards

explanation.surface: Restrict which emblem the island of Martinique adopts.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is a hindrance, and to trammel is to hamper or confine, a synonym for restrict.

clue.text: Hat small boy's shown around street occasionally

indicators.note: the small boy pieces surround the letters taken from street

parts.note: a son is a male child, a boy

indicators.note: only every other letter of street is used

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the word are the ones kept

explanation.surface: A little boy's hat is shown off around the street now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, so it is an example of headwear.

clue.text: Sites where hearts may be touched by likeable comments?

definitions.text: Sites where hearts may be touched
definitions.meaning: emotionally moving places, but also websites where heart icons are tapped
posts that people like, in the online sense

explanation.walkthrough: Being touched suggests emotion; online, people tap a heart icon to like a comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Platforms such as Instagram are websites where users like posts and comments by tapping hearts.

clue.text: Insults City for waterlogged pitch, perhaps

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mudslinging
Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: Fans hurl insults at a City team over a soggy pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: City looks like a football club; it is the English spa city of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A sodden, churned-up playing field is jokingly likened to a spa bath of wet earth.

clue.text: Give grandee bananas and pineapple

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Offer a nobleman bananas and a pineapple, like a fruit basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit theme hides that pineapple is old military slang for a grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple was soldiers' slang for a grenade because of the ridged casing's shape.

clue.text: Manage to check the face of Scheffler's wood

indicators.note: checking holds back, so the first letter is held within

parts.note: to cope is to manage

indicators.note: the front of the golfer's name, its initial

parts.note: the golfer's name supplies just its initial

explanation.surface: A golfer manages to check the face of Scottie Scheffler's wooden club.
explanation.walkthrough: Scottie Scheffler is a golfer, and a wood is a golf club; here wood means a small group of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Maid leans on the rocks, one charming the opposite sex

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A maid leans on the rocks, perhaps drunk, while someone flirts with her.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who is popular with and attentive to women is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Adult with free and singular relations

parts.note: A is the old British film certificate for adult
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: An adult who is free and single among the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, the sisters of one's parents, so aunties are relations.

clue.text: For all fit ponies: jumping

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something done for all the fit ponies that are show-jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For all' reads as 'for everyone'; it is the phrase meaning 'despite'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For all his efforts' means despite them, so the two prepositional phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Solver intends to noisily put down chocolate cake

indicators.note: the words are heard aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: the solver is 'you', and intending is 'will', so together 'you'll'
to log something is to record it, write it down

explanation.surface: A solver plans to loudly turn down a chocolate cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is a homophone: 'you'll' said out loud gives the festive word; the record-keeping word is spelt as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas pudding alternative, it is a chocolate sponge roll decorated to look like a tree branch.

clue.text: Tap with very quiet drip

parts.note: to milk is to tap or draw off a resource
so is used as an intensifier, as in 'so good'
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A tap with a very quiet drip.
explanation.walkthrough: The plumbing picture hides that a drip is a feeble, wet person.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a weak, spineless person, the same as calling someone a drip.

clue.text: Point above extremely tenacious insects

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a locus is a particular point or position

indicators.note: only the very ends of tenacious are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A point raised about extremely tenacious insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are grasshoppers that swarm, so they are a kind of insect.

clue.text: People vaping in steam trains?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those puffing on e-cigarettes
second meaning: a childish name for steam locomotives, which puff smoke

explanation.surface: People vaping on steam trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that blows out clouds, a smoker or a chuffing engine, can be described by this nursery word.

clue.text: One's first wife wearing wig and leather

indicators.note: the inner letters are clothed by the word for wig

parts.note: to wig is an old word for scolding, so it means chide

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word one is used

parts.note: the word supplies only its initial

explanation.surface: One's first wife wearing a wig and leather outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wig' looks like a hairpiece; it is the verb meaning to rebuke, as in a wigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowhide is leather made from a cow's skin.

clue.text: Found in chancel, estate's musical instrument

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters across the two words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An estate's musical instrument is discovered in the church chancel.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Moving slowly, arresting missing leader of pack

indicators.note: the word lacks the letter that follows

parts.note: to pinch is slang for to arrest

indicators.note: the leader of a group goes at its head, so the opening letter of pack

parts.note: the word supplies only its initial

explanation.surface: Police moving slowly, arresting the gang leader who is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to advance by tiny amounts, so inching is creeping along.

clue.text: Deft clue? I could be lying!

indicators.note: the letters could be turned into something else, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a deft clue, then admits they could be lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deceitful means given to deceiving, so it is a synonym for lying as an adjective.

clue.text: Seed, firm and earthy? Not half!

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for earthy is kept

parts.note: earthy humour is coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A seed, firm and earthy? Not half! — a gardener's emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like the British exclamation meaning 'very much so'; here it drops half a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa beans are the seeds of the cacao tree, so the word can name the seed itself.

clue.text: Blanket put over one raccoon-like mammal

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: a blanket of snow is a coat of it

explanation.surface: A blanket is put over a single raccoon-like mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted American mammal of the raccoon family.

clue.text: Basic American uniform and unopened berets sent back

indicators.note: the remaining letters are returned in reverse
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Basic American uniforms, with the unopened berets returned to the supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means plain and without adornment, a synonym for basic.

clue.text: When fish can be seen on south-east coast

indicators.note: in an across clue, the following letters come after the abbreviation

parts.note: as in 'as I arrived' means when
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A time when fish are visible on England's south-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coastal area by the sea, so it names the coast.

clue.text: Fan to gossip about using excessive flattery

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into another order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan is ready to gossip about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is smooth persuasive praise, so soft-soaping is buttering someone up.
